strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas Timedelta/to_timedelta bug (GH#66247, GH#63275): for float inf/-inf and for overflowing round floats with coarse units, buggy code raises a bare OverflowError (not caught by errors="coerce") instead of OutOfBoundsTimedelta (ValueError), so the added tests fail. The fixed revision routes non-finite floats via is_integer() gating and wraps overflow to raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta, so tests pass.

pinned_because: NumPy is numerically relevant and uncapped in the provided evidence; choose a representative NumPy from the supported range for maximal chance of matching the buggy overflow behavior, but exact minimum/maximum versions are not stated in the evidence.
pandas build depends on Cython for compiling extensions; evidence marks it as a documented dependency but provides no version constraints, so install the latest available for the environment.

strategy.reproducing_test: Run the three tests shown in test_command against the buggy commit 20542d17b1cc, then repeat on the fixed commit (the PR’s merge commit after 20542d17b1cc) and verify the expected transition: buggy revision fails by raising OverflowError / not producing NaT under errors="coerce", while fixed revision passes by raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta and returning NaT for errors="coerce".
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 20542d17b1cc: test_float_inf_raises and/or test_round_float_overflow_unit fail because Timedelta(val) / Timedelta(1e19, unit="s") raise a bare OverflowError instead of OutOfBoundsTimedelta (ValueError), and test_to_timedelta_object_inf fails because to_timedelta(arr, errors="coerce") does not produce NaT for inf/-inf (or to_timedelta(arr) raises the wrong exception type). On fixed revision: all three tests pass—inf/-inf and overflowing round floats with coarse units raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta (match "without overflow"), and errors="coerce" converts inf/-inf elements to NaT (so the array/object-array coercion test passes).
strategy.numerical_probe: (Not a separate numeric check; the tests themselves act as the oracle by asserting exception type/behavior and that errors="coerce" yields NaT.)
